blocks.content: The Central Information Commission is a high-powered independent body that inter alia looks into the complaints made to it and decides the appeals.

rows: Fixed term of 5 years (or up to age 65)
Prescribed by Central Govt (currently 3 years, up to age 65)
Equivalent to Chief Election Commissioner / Election Commissioners
Determined directly by the Central Government
Salaries reduced by amount of previous pension/retirement benefits
Provisions for pension deductions were removed

items: The CIC is a statutory body, NOT a constitutional body.
Under the RTI Amendment Act 2019, the tenure, salaries, and service conditions of Information Commissioners are determined by the Central Government rather than fixed statutory terms.
While inquiring, the Commission has the powers of a civil court in respect of summoning persons, requiring discovery of documents, and receiving evidence on affidavit.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Central Information Commission (CIC) was constituted in 2005 under the provisions of the Right to Information Act, 2005.
The Commission consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners.

Members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
The Chief Information Commissioner and Information Commissioners are not eligible for reappointment.
The Commission submits an annual report to the Central Government, which is laid before each House of Parliament.
